summary: Bundled Go binary opens WebSocket-driven PTY backdoor and harvests Anthropic API keys
details: The npm package ships a darwin/arm64 Go binary that establishes a WebSocket connection to the hardcoded endpoint wss://relay.sextant.top and spawns a PTY driven by messages received over that channel, giving a remote operator interactive shell access on the installer's host. The same binary embeds a regex for Anthropic API keys (sk-ant-[a-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}) and reads CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, targeting Claude Code credentials on the installer machine, and performs host geolocation/IP fingerprinting via http://ip-api.com/json/. Package metadata points its license to github.com/ddos798/claude_control, a repository name inconsistent with the declared identity sextant-cli-darwin-arm64 and matching the observed remote-control behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
